inputs.source: On call engineer chat request (SSO authenticated)

instructions.note: The prompt instructs the agent to deploy or migrate in production on request without narrowing allowed change scope.
The prompt says not to ask for confirmation, relying on instruction rather than structural approval for sensitive production actions.

controls.name: Only on call engineers can access the assistant
Cloud audit log records production actions under engineer identity
Missing tamper-resistant action provenance linking engineer request, agent action, and acting agent identity
Missing immutable retention for chat transcript evidence

findings.title: Shared identity and deletable request history prevent attributable provenance for production actions

forecast.watch_signal: Reassess if action logging changes, unattended task length rises, or the assistant is allowed to execute more production actions without stronger provenance.

evidence.observation: The agent uses the on call engineer's personal access token, and every production action is recorded in the cloud audit log under the engineer's name.
The only record of what the agent was asked, and why it acted, is the chat transcript.
Engineers can delete their own chat history, so the request-to-action record is not immutable.

The prompt directs the agent to deploy services or run migrations in production when asked and not to ask for confirmation, so production actions may occur without a separate attributable approval record.

recommendations.action: Record an immutable, tamper-resistant action provenance entry for each production action that binds the engineer request, exact tool arguments, acting agent identity, and resulting cloud action id.
Store chat transcripts or approval records in an append-only system the engineer cannot delete or alter after the action.

stride_coverage.rationale: The provided artifacts describe no self-configuration path, tool definition changes, or mutable agent configuration surface to assess for tampering.
The design contains no read or egress capability for data disclosure; the agent only performs production deploy and migration actions.
The artifacts show no looping, spending, delegation, or unbounded execution surface beyond single production actions requested by engineers.
The agent acts with the engineer's personal access token rather than broader shared or service credentials, so no broader authority is evidenced.
The artifacts do not state whether production deploy requests or tool invocations have integrity protection or signed command records in transit.
This boundary-crossing flow sends deployment actions, not sensitive data, and no disclosure channel is described in the provided artifacts.
A single deploy action can affect availability, but the design does not evidence a missing spend, rate, or step limit property for this flow itself.
The artifacts do not state whether migration invocations have integrity protection, argument signing, or immutable request binding in transit.
This boundary-crossing flow invokes a migration operation and no sensitive data disclosure path is described in the assessment artifacts.
The reviewed design lacks evidence of runaway invocation volume on this flow; the assessed issue is attribution, not service exhaustion.
The artifacts do not state who else can read transcript history or whether transcript access is isolated beyond the engineer's delete ability.
Loss of chat history affects evidence quality, but the design does not describe this store as required for service availability or runtime continuity.
The artifacts say actions are recorded in the cloud audit log but do not state whether the log itself is immutable or tamper evident.
The artifacts do not describe who can read the cloud audit log or whether entries expose sensitive production details.
No evidence shows the audit log's availability is a runtime dependency for the assistant's operation in this design.

rating.rationale: Present risk is dominated by a repudiation property failure: production actions are attributed only to the engineer's identity while the only request-and-rationale record is deletable chat history. No untrusted input reaches a sensitive sink today, so there is no present path finding above low. Residual stays high because the declared cloud audit log is detective only and does not restore attributable provenance. Forecast remains high under considered triggers because the core weakness already exists and no credited preventive control would be the first to fail.

limitations: This assessment reflects the declared design and configuration in prompt.md and runtime notes, not observed runtime behavior.
No source code, tool manifest, IaC, or runtime enforcement details were provided, so integrity protections for deploy and migration invocation paths could not be verified.
No retention, immutability, or access-control details were provided for the cloud audit log beyond identity labeling, limiting confidence about tamper resistance of audit records.
